rows.headline: PB Fintech posts 42% rise in Q2 net profit to Rs 192 crore
rows.hook: Strong quarter drives PB Fintech net profit up
rows.summary: PB Fintech reported a 42.5% jump in consolidated net profit to ₹192.4 Cr for the September quarter of FY27, compared to ₹135 Cr in the same period last year. Revenue from operations grew 35% during the quarter, reflecting strong performance across its core insurance and lending platforms. The company operates digital insurance and credit marketplaces like Policybazaar and Paisabazaar. rows.headline: SIS Group founder and former BJP leader RK Sinha dies
rows.hook: SIS Group founder passes away at 75
rows.summary: Ravindra Kishore Sinha, the founder of security services firm SIS Group, has passed away at the age of 75. A former Rajya Sabha member and BJP leader, Sinha built SIS into one of India's largest security and facility management companies. The company is listed on the Indian stock exchanges and provides services across India and Australia. His passing marks the end of a significant tenure in the private security industry.

rows.headline: Punjab records 1,007 stubble burning cases with over Rs 17 lakh in fines
rows.hook: Stubborn stubble burning persists across Punjab
rows.summary: Punjab authorities have registered 1,007 stubble burning incidents across the state, levying fines exceeding Rs 17 lakh against violators. Stubble burning remains a persistent contributor to severe winter air pollution in northern India, impacting air quality indices across the region. While direct corporate impact is limited, worsening air quality often triggers administrative clampdowns and agricultural policy debates. Indian retail investors should note how prolonged agricultural pollution can influence regional economic activity and regulatory scrutiny on farming practices.
rows.whats_next: Daily stubble burning count updates through peak harvest season
rows.why_it_matters: Worsening air quality risks strict administrative curbs and regional disruptions

rows.headline: Government plans new social security benefits for gig workers
rows.hook: New social security framework for gig workers
rows.summary: The Indian government is formulating a new policy to provide social security benefits to gig workers, including delivery partners and cab drivers. The proposed framework aims to extend protections such as insurance, health benefits, and retirement savings to those working for platforms like Zomato, Swiggy, Ola, and Uber. This move follows growing concerns over the lack of formal employment benefits for the rapidly expanding gig economy workforce. The policy is expected to formalize working conditions and provide a safety net for millions of platform-based employees.
rows.whats_next: Official draft policy notification and stakeholder consultations
rows.why_it_matters: Platform companies may face higher operational costs due to mandatory contributions.
rows.winners_losers: Gig workers gain / Platform companies face costs
